pr_body:
![TabSwitchingv2](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/57155886/88237962-5505d500-cc35-11ea-8384-d91699155067.gif)

## Summary of the Pull Request
This PR adds the Advanced Tab Switcher (ATS) to Terminal. It'll work
similarly to VSCode's tab switcher. Because this implementation rides
off a lot of the Command Palette's XAML code, it'll look just like the
Command Palette, and also have support for tab title search.

## References
#3753 - ATS Spec

Closes #1502

Design feedback: (full review in progress)

I fricken love that you got the icons figured out. Now we can follow up by letting commands specify the icon too! (not in this PR for sure)

I agree that they maybe need a tad bit more spacing. 

I'm not sure I love the labels for `Index:0` etc. 

Maybe change the `Type a command name...` string depending on which mode we're in?

> I'm not sure I love the labels for `Index:0` etc.

Same, I'm not sure what it should look like otherwise though. Also the index is kinda the only identifying information to differentiate tabs with the same titles from each other. 😞 -- Definitely open to ideas from the team on how to present it!

> consolidate

I mean, they’re already the same thing with different entry points; how much more consolidated do you want them, @WSLUser?

Please do not inundate Leon's pull request with unrelated comments.
Thanks!

Love all the new stuff in 1.3.  Great job

Russ

>We'd love feedback on why the new tab switcher didn't work for you!

Not sure where this feedback should go, this seems like a reasonable place. I found it distracting to pop up on <kbd>ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>tab</kbd> every time, so I turned it off. 

I do find the list of tabs to be valuable, but would prefer it to be accessible with a separate key (I guess that's the `tabSearch` action, which I have bound to <kbd>ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>`</kbd>).

Strongly agree with @simonratner on the Advanced Tab Switcher - when I press <kbd>ctrl+tab</kbd> or <kbd>ctrl+shift+tab</kbd>, I just want to go to the next/previous tab, not get a modal popup. The `tabSearch` action does seem to be a better application of this functionality in terms of having a way to efficiently navigate through large numbers of open tabs.

Having said that, I thought the implementation of Advanced Tab Switcher was very clean. And since you exposed the `useTabSwitcher` setting, we can all just enable/disable the feature as desired.

You guys rock. Please keep making Windows Terminal great!

issue_context.title: Feature Request: An advanced tab switcher
issue_context.body: "Another option would be to make a keyboard driven tab switcher that shows a dialog list of the tabs in a vertical list with their current active paths.  Horizontally expanding things don't work well with the terminal and most of the tabs are off the edge of the screen and effectively invisible.   At the moment the ALT key + number is a tab switcher.  It would be super cool if you pressed ALT this list of tabs would popup, you could see all your tabs, then complete your ALT chord with the number you are wanting."
comments: something that makes things a little better for powershell, is that you can set the window title with $host.UI.RawUI.WindowTitle = ""    or  you can hook the prompt to set it to the current directory as per https://devblogs.microsoft.com/powershell/setting-the-console-title-to-be-your-current-working-directory/
Thanks for the request. _please_ make sure to search for existing issues! #597 #608 cover tab sizing and titling. We should repurpose this one to just be the request for an enhanced tab switcher.

yes, I did see those, it just didn't quite capture what I wanted. Horizontal tabs are going to be a huge UI problem hence why tab size  is a problem in those issues.   I don't mind the the exact solution, but any way to quickly see your tabs in a vertical list seems a big improvement.    At the moment I have a script that just sets my powershell titles to be my current path ( will need some work to trim it down for long paths) and I can fit a few, but I can't do that with my other shells ( that I know of)

just FYI for anyone else who wants nicer tabs for powershell,

in my %UserProfile%\My Documents\WindowsPowerShell\Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1

I put

Function Prompt {
    $host.UI.RawUI.WindowTitle = Get-Location
    "$(Get-Location)> "
}

I'm switching this over to be the "advanced tab switcher" feature request and putting it on our backlog.

review_comments: Have you tried `LayoutUpdated`? It might be better for a oneshot event for when the listview is "ready" :smile:

I tried `LayoutUpdated` at first, but it seemed like events were being received by the handler even before I've even opened the CmdPal/ATS for the first time. I think it's because `LayoutUpdated` fires if anything in the visual tree causes the control to change their "layout"? So I tried `SizeChanged` like the docs said to if I wanted to listen to something more specific to the control and it seems to work.

Huh, out of curiosity, how does this command work in the command palette? If there's an anchor key specified for `tabSwitcher`, but the user isn't pressing it, then does it just auto close? In that case, should we just return an empty string whenever there's an anchor key (effectively hiding this command)?

If there's not an anchor key set, does Command Palette -> Tab Switcher work as smoothly as I hope it does?

That's a good point, the anchor mode will pop up and not disappear bc there's no KeyUpEvent detected. I do agree on hiding anchor mode from the palette though, it doesn't make much sense to toggle it in that way.

I also found a related bug where toggling the non-anchor mode thru the palette doesn't work because the action that's dispatched  finishes before `_close()` is called inside of `_dispatchCommand()`, I'll have to add that to my TODOs.
